kind.description: Kind is program for a program; absent for an LLM routine (llm).

executable.description: Executable is the app's copy, the one that runs.

checksum.description: Checksum is the executable's SHA-256 (trust is keyed to it).

writes.description:
Writes is whether it can change anything: a dry run passes it
--dry-run; one that doesn't write runs as it is.

env.description: Env is the environment variable it's passed as.

items.description: ProgramSecret is a secret a program declares, and whether it's stored (`auth login <program>` stores it).

program.description:
Program is what trusting a program approves: the executable that
runs (by checksum, with its description file), what it declares.

items.description: CheckedTool is an allowlisted tool as a routine would get it.

tools.description:
Tools are its allowlisted tools with the server offering each and
whether it's read-only (absent when its servers couldn't be reached).

toolsError.description:
ToolsError says why its tools couldn't be checked (e.g. a server needs
a sign-in).

changes.description: Changes since it was last trusted (empty for a first trust).

resumed.description:
Resumed is true when --resume turned its schedule on (it was paused),
or turned a hook on.

hook.description:
Hook is true for a hook: Kind is its action's, and Trigger is what it
acts on, which trusting it covers too.

label.description:
Label is what its type means, as its watcher declares it ("End key
pressed"): set by the app from the watcher, never written in a hook's
file. Absent when it has no type, or its watcher declares none.

on.description:
On is a hook's trigger as `hooks list` gives it: with its type's
label, as its watcher declares it.

untrusted.description: Untrusted says why not (no such watcher, not trusted yet, changed).

description.description:
Description, Mode and Program are what it is and runs (absent when
there's no such watcher): its executable by checksum, its arguments
and secrets, each stored or not.

executable.description: Executable is the app's copy, the one that runs.

checksum.description: Checksum is the executable's SHA-256 (trust is keyed to it).

writes.description:
Writes is whether it can change anything: a dry run passes it
--dry-run; one that doesn't write runs as it is.

env.description: Env is the environment variable it's passed as.

items.description: ProgramSecret is a secret a program declares, and whether it's stored (`auth login <program>` stores it).

label.description: Label is what it means, in words ("End key pressed").

hooks.description:
Hooks are the hooks that act on it: those listening for its type, and
those listening for every type.

items.description: WatcherEvent is an event a watcher declares, with the hooks that act on it.

events.description:
Events are the events it declares it prints, which trusting it
covers (absent: it declares none, and may print any type).

changes.description: Changes since it was last trusted (empty for a first trust).

watcher.description:
Watcher is the hook's watcher: trusting the hook (--yes) trusts it
too when it isn't trusted, so its review is part of the hook's.

warnings.description:
Warnings are what to weigh before trusting it: an LLM hook with
write tools acts on outside event data.

signIns.description:
SignIns are the sign-ins it still needs before it works (`auth login
<name>`): its servers', its own secrets' (a program's, a hook's), and
its watcher's. Trusting doesn't wait for them.

label.description: Label is what the OS calls it (Input Monitoring).

state.description:
State is what the scheduler last found: granted, missing, unknown (it
can't be checked), unsupported (not on this OS) or not-checked
(nothing recorded yet). Only missing and not-checked keep it from
running.

items.description: PermissionSource is what declares a permission something needs: a plugin it uses, its own program (a program's, a program hook's) or its watcher.

where.description:
Where says where it's turned on, following "turn it on" ("in System
Settings > Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring"), and SettingsURL is
the address that opens it (absent where there's none).

items.description: PermissionNeed is a permission something needs, what declares it, and what the scheduler last found.

permissions.description:
Permissions are what the OS must allow it before it works: an LLM
routine's plugins', a program's own, a hook's action's and its
watcher's, each with what declares it and what the scheduler last
found (`permissions request <permission>` asks for one). Trusting
covers them (one added later needs a new review) and doesn't wait for
them; while one isn't granted it doesn't run.
